reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is a consumer technology tutorial explaining Samsung Galaxy dual VoLTE, including a reported limitation involving dual-SIM data settings and a related software update. The visuals show SIM Card Manager entries for Jio and Airtel and a system-update screen, although the sampled frames do not establish the update's final technical outcome. The request to follow or subscribe is ordinary channel engagement and is not presented as a condition for payment, investment, credentials, or another financial offer.

citations.quote: Samsung Galaxy S9+ Dual VoLTE enabled, plus what is Dual VoLTE?
In this video I have explained what Dual VoLTE is and what happens when dual VoLTE is not enabled.
The update size if 426MB.
In this video, I'll tell you about the benefits of dual-voltage and what it does.
I go into SIM card manager

opening.argument: Judge, the video does more than explain a setting. It presents a desirable capability as the result of a simple viewer action: "Update the handset and after that dual VoLTE will be enabled." The payoff is framed concretely as being able to use both SIMs together, including two Jio SIMs. That promise-action pairing is the strongest reason to scrutinize the video as a solicitation for an easy-to-obtain benefit, even though the action is packaged as routine maintenance.

citations.quote: Update the handset and after that dual VoLTE will be enabled.
But with this Samsung Galaxy S9+ dual VoLTE support I am now able to use both SIM together, in fact you can use 2 JIO SIMs together.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The explanation and SIM settings cited by the defense establish the topic, but they do not settle the role of the instruction to update. Nor does the absence of a payment request answer whether the promised capability is being used to drive an action. The video explicitly connects that action to the claimed benefit.

citations.quote: Update the handset and after that dual VoLTE will be enabled.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The promised benefit is ordinary phone functionality delivered through a software update, not a cash payment, claimable asset, or withdrawal. The video identifies the update as a change to the handset and explains the prior dual-SIM limitation. Telling owners to update their phones does not, by itself, establish a deceptive acquisition scheme.

citations.quote: I also updated the handset my Samsung Galaxy S9+, the latest software update now enabled Dual VoLTE and VoWiFi (Voice over Wi-Fi).
Without Dual VoLTE support on Samsung Galaxy S9+ I was not able to use JIO SIM when I enabled data on my airtel SIM

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation combines a time-sensitive update prompt with a confident benefit claim. The speaker says viewers may already have an update notification, then directs them to update for dual VoLTE. Yet the sampled installation image shows the update still at 25%; that image alone cannot verify the promised result. The description also points viewers to other video links and the channel asks them to subscribe. None of those signals proves deception individually, but together they warrant closer scrutiny of how confidently the benefit is sold.

citations.quote: If you are using the Samsung Galaxy S9 or the S9+ you might have got the update notification. Update the handset and after that dual VoLTE will be enabled.
Best Smartphones that you can buy in India https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v3GdwXl8MxE&list=PLD4rZCdlPoa30yC2ynOJ0HZjsUwrzrXTw

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense concedes that sampled frames do not establish the final technical outcome. That matters when the description asserts the update enables the feature and urges viewers to install it. Showing a settings screen and an update in progress supports the tutorial framing, but neither independently verifies every claimed post-update capability.

citations.quote: Update the handset and after that dual VoLTE will be enabled.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A frame captured during installation is not evidence that the later claim is false. The speaker also says the update has been installed and describes trying to dial from the Jio SIM afterward. The supplied links are to other videos, while the subscribe request is channel engagement; neither supplies a reward-claim flow or financial inducement.

citations.quote: So, here's the new update that came in, it's now installed on this handset. I go into SIM card manager
And now I'm trying to dial from Jio SIM.

opening.argument: Judge, the educational framing also functions as promotion of a specific outcome. The title announces that dual VoLTE is enabled, the description tells owners to update, and the claimed benefit is that both SIM slots can support 4G together. The walkthrough gives that recommendation practical force by first describing a Jio SIM that stops working when Airtel data is enabled. Read this way, the explanation is not merely background information; it steers viewers from a frustrating problem toward the proposed update.

citations.quote: Samsung Galaxy S9+ Dual VoLTE enabled, plus what is Dual VoLTE?
Update the handset and after that dual VoLTE will be enabled.
Now both SIM 1 and SIM 2 slot support 4G together.
every time I enable the data I have on Airtel, the SIM I have on Jio is deactivated

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's account of a tutorial is compatible with the video steering behavior: explaining the SIM limitation makes the recommendation more persuasive. Its cited title and explanation describe the subject, but do not erase the explicit direction to update or the benefit attached to doing so.

citations.quote: Update the handset and after that dual VoLTE will be enabled.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The recommendation follows directly from the operational issue being demonstrated. The description says what the update changes, while the speaker discusses SIM behavior before and after installation. Promotion of a useful phone update is not evidence of a scam without a deceptive promise or an acquisition flow; the cited material establishes neither.
